10.1002/adfm.79467.abstract: The following paper sets out the design, synthesis, and schematic illustration of the photocatalytic nitrogen fixation mechanism of FeMnMOF photocatalysts with single-atom Mn─N sites. Among the prepared catalysts, U-FeMnMOF demonstrated the most effective photocatalytic nitrogen fixation capacity, with an ammonia yield of 1823.1 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 . ABSTRACT Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction involves complex proton-coupled multi-electron transfer processes, which bring about abundant reaction pathways and thus result in poorly controllable product selectivity. Benefiting from their unique electronic configuration and unsaturated coordination environment, single-atom photocatalysts can effectively regulate the reaction pathways of photoreductive N 2 activation and reduction, thereby improving the selectivity and NH 3 productivity of target ammonia products. Herein, an acetate-modified ultrasonication method is developed to construct atomically dispersed, coordinatively unsaturated Mn–N sites on Fe-based metal–organic frameworks (FeMOFs). Distinct from traditional carbon-based single-atom catalysts, these Mn─N sites are fabricated via a mild wet-chemistry approach without high-temperature treatment. The optimized U-FeMnMOF(Fe:Mn = 1:3) achieves a high NH 3 productivity of 1823.1 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 , 21.2 times that of pure FeMOF. Characterizations and DFT results verify that Mn─N sites not only activate N 2 and optimize hydrogen adsorption, but also work as a charge transfer mediator to form a direct Z-scheme heterojunction. This study presents a feasible strategy to synthesize non-carbon M─N single-atom catalysts for efficient PNRR.

10.1002/adsc.70858.abstract: Photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia holds dual significance for nitrogen‐containing wastewater remediation and green ammonia synthesis. However, single‐component semiconductor photocatalysts are generally hampered by severe photogenerated charge recombination, insufficient spectral response, and poor substrate activation. Herein, cobalt porphyrin (CoTCPP) was in situ anchored onto the surface of Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 nanorods via a solvothermal method to construct CoTCPP/Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 photocatalysts featuring strong interfacial coupling. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis reveals a distinct interfacial electronic coupling between CoTCPP and Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 . This strong interfacial coupling synergistically enhances photocatalytic performance by facilitating rapid capture and efficient interfacial transfer of photogenerated electrons to effectively suppress charge carrier recombination, significantly broadening the near‐infrared (NIR) light response range, and strengthening the electrostatic adsorption of NO 3 − on the catalyst surface to accelerate the selective generation of NH 3 . The optimized 1.5CoTCPP/Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 achieved an NH 3 production rate of 1230.81 μmol·g −1 ·h −1 , approximately 5‐fold higher than that of pristine Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 . In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the stepwise deoxygenation–hydrogenation reduction pathway of NO 3 − → *NO 3 → *NO 2 → *NO → *NHOH → *NH 2 OH → NH 3 . This work provides an effective strategy for constructing interfacially coupled photocatalytic systems toward efficient nitrate reduction to ammonia.

10.1002/aenm.71791.abstract: Light irradiation dynamically generates oxygen vacancies at Ni/CeO 2 interfaces, forming Ce–Ov–Ni motifs that promote NH 3 adsorption and N–H activation while directing hydrogen intermediates to Ni sites. Vacancy-induced electronic modulation weakens H 2 adsorption, accelerates hydrogen release, mitigates hydrogen poisoning, and enables efficient low-temperature photothermal NH 3 -to-H 2 conversion. ABSTRACT NH 3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H 2 release is hindered by N–H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle-supported CeO 2 (Ni/CeO 2 ) for low-temperature photothermal NH 3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO 2 , which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce–Ov–Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH 3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen-vacancy-associated sites favor NH 3 adsorption, N–H bond activation, and N-containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy-induced electronic modulation weakens H 2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H 2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N- and H-containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO 2 achieves 96.3% NH 3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat −1 ·h −1 . It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat −1 ·min −1 H 2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light-induced oxygen-vacancy–metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen-poisoning-resistant NH 3 -to-H 2 conversion.

10.1002/anie.2196422.abstract: An electron bridge strategy is developed to regulate charge polarization in Pd 1 and Ni 1 dual single-atom sites, promoting CO 2 reduction, nitrate reduction, and C–N coupling simultaneously. The resulting catalyst achieves efficient urea electrosynthesis with high activity and record durability over 1700 h. ABSTRACT Urea electrosynthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrates powered by green electricity is a zero-carbon route for urea production. Simultaneously achieving high activity and long-term stability is a prerequisite for the industrialization of urea electrosynthesis. In this study, we propose an electron bridge strategy based on a Pd 1 and Ni 1 dual single-atom alloy to boost the electrocatalytic activity and durability for urea electrosynthesis. The single-atom Ni 1 sites act as electron bridges to promote charge transfer from Cu to Pd 1 sites, leading to charge-polarized Pd–Cu sites, which upshift the d-band center and improve oxidation resistance of the catalyst. Consequently, the Pd 1 and Ni 1 dual single-atom sites simultaneously accelerates both carbon dioxide reduction and nitrates reduction half-reactions, while facilitating the first C–N coupling step. The Pd 1 and Ni 1 dual single-atom alloys deliver a urea yield rate of 541.6 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a urea Faradaic efficiency of 57.3%. Remarkably, this catalyst achieves a record durability of 1700 h at a current density of 40 mA cm −2 . This work provides new insights into the synergistic catalysis of complex multi-molecule reactions through cooperative multiple active sites.

10.1002/anie.3751410.abstract: Nitro functional group was incorporated into NiFe-MOF ligands near metal sites, which undergo a simple and direct oxidation to NO 3 − and subsequently anchored on the reconstructed γ-NiFeOOH phase. The anchored NO 3 − not only forms a robust Cl − -repelling interface but also activates lattice oxygen to drive the efficient lattice-oxygen-mediated pathway for active and durable seawater electrolysis. ABSTRACT Chloride ions (Cl − )-induced corrosion severely limits the practical implementation of direct seawater electrolysis. Although oxyanion incorporation can mitigate Cl − poisoning, existing approaches offer limited control over oxyanion generation and retention during catalyst reconstruction. Herein, we report a MOF-based ligand-engineering strategy that enables defined oxyanion incorporation into reconstructed metal oxyhydroxides for active and durable seawater electrolysis. Nitro- (NO 2 ) functionalized ligands are incorporated into a NiFe-MOF precursor, where the NO 2 group undergo a simple and direct oxidation to nitrate (NO 3 − ) during electrochemical reconstruction, enabling well-defined NO 3 − regulation of the reconstructed γ-NiFeOOH phase. The anchored NO 3 − not only forms a robust Cl − -repelling interface but also activates lattice oxygen to drive a mechanistic transition from an adsorbate evolution mechanism to a more efficient lattice-oxygen-mediated pathway. The designed catalyst achieves excellent oxygen evolution reaction performance in alkaline seawater, requiring an overpotential of only 230 mV to reach a current density of 500 mA cm −2 , outperforming its NO 3 − -free counterpart. It also exhibits high durability, operating for over 4000 h at 1.5 A cm −2 with an ultralow degradation rate of 1.8 µV h −1 . Furthermore, a kilowatt-level alkaline seawater electrolyzer equipped with the designed electrode operates stably for over 1100 h under industrially relevant conditions.

10.1002/anie.7471326.abstract: Embedding hydrazone photoswitches into hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks enables sequential, programmable macroscopic optical outputs. Ammonia exposure unlocks solid-state E / Z photoisomerization, which triggers a cascade reorganization of TPE packing to modulate coloration and luminescence, providing a design paradigm for high-security, information-dense smart photofunctional materials. ABSTRACT Light-driven molecular switches enable precise and noninvasive regulation of molecular structure and function, and thus represent fundamental building blocks for stimuli-responsive photofunctional materials. However, translating molecular-level photoswitching into sequence-dependent macroscopic outputs in the solid state remains a formidable challenge. In this study, we report a supramolecular strategy that integrates guanyl hydrazone switches into hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) to overcome this limitation. A tetrasulfonate-substituted tetraphenylethylene anion ( TPE 4 − ) is employed as the host scaffold, while guanyl hydrazone ( G2 ) functions as the photoresponsive guest, affording a functional framework through cooperative assembly. This system leverages a reversible crystalline–amorphous phase transformation, triggered by acid–base stimuli, to gate the solid-state photoisomerization of G2 . Upon activation, the configurational switching of G2 induces a cascade reorganization of the TPE 4 − packing motifs, leading to pronounced and sequence-dependent modulation of both fluorescence and macroscopic coloration. In addition, the applicability of this system in information encryption has been demonstrated. This work expands the design paradigm of hydrazone-based photoswitches in the solid state and provides a supramolecular strategy for constructing intelligent optical materials with high information density and enhanced security.

10.1002/chem.71875.abstract: ABSTRACT The production of hydrogen from chemical hydrides has garnered significant interest as a sustainable method for producing clean energy. The hydrolysis of ammonia borane (NH 3 BH 3 , AB) under mild reaction conditions was assessed in this work using a highly active Ru–Ni alloy catalyst supported on CeO 2 . As‐synthesized Ru–Ni/CeO 2 with different metal contents was used as a heterogeneous catalyst for the mild hydrolytic dehydrogenation of AB. At 298 K, the optimal catalyst is Ru 0.5 Ni 1.25 /CeO 2 , which demonstrated exceptional catalytic activity with a TOF value of 1226.0 mol H2 min − 1 . The calculated apparent activation energy was 37.5 kJ mol −1 , which is even lower than that of the majority of noble‐metal‐based catalysts for AB dehydrogenation. Strong electronic interactions and synergistic effects between Ru and Ni led to the formation of a bimetallic alloy structure with increased catalytic activity when Ni was incorporated into Ru. The dispersion and stability of the nanoparticles were enhanced by CeO 2 ’s strong metal–support interactions, and high oxygen storage capacity, which made it an efficient support. Additionally, after several catalytic cycles, the catalyst showed exceptional structural stability with little activity loss. This study demonstrates the potential of Ru–Ni/CeO 2 as an economical and effective catalyst for applications involving the production of hydrogen.

10.1002/cssc.71193.abstract: LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cathode material has attracted considerable attention because of its potential to achieve substantially higher energy densities, but the practical deployment of NCM811 remains hindered by severe interfacial and structural degradation during repeated cycling. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) was employed in this study to construct an amorphous Li─Si─O (LSO) coating layer with different thicknesses on the surface of NCM811 cathode materials, and their effects on the structural characteristics, interfacial properties, and electrochemical performance were systematically investigated. Among all the samples, 50 LSO@NCM811 exhibits the best electrochemical performance, retaining a discharge capacity of 115.96 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles at 1 C under a cutoff voltage of 4.3 V. By constructing a stable and ionically conductive interfacial protective layer, the LSO coating achieves the synergistic optimization of interfacial stability, structural stability, and electrochemical kinetics, thereby markedly enhancing the electrochemical performance of NCM811 cathode materials. This work provides important insights into interfacial engineering design for high‐nickel layered cathode materials of lithium‐ion batteries.

10.1002/elt2.70075.abstract: ABSTRACT The photochemical reduction of nitrogen offers an environmentally friendly approach for ammonia synthesis, providing an alternative to the energy‐intensive and emission‐heavy Haber–Bosch process. Despite its promise, the process is impeded by slow nitrogen activation and excessive hydrogen evolution. To overcome these limitations, we present a tandem nickel phthalocyanine (NiPc)/CNT‐P&Cu‐BCN photocatalyst, engineered with an organic–organic heterojunction for enhanced nitrogen conversion. This system integrates boron‐doped (B), nitrogen‐deficient (N) carbon nitride (CN), modified via Cu–Cu coordination and phosphorus doping through sodium borohydride‐assisted thermal treatment, with hydrogen‐bonded, ultrathin NiPc nanosheets. This novel design yields a record ammonia production rate of 915.4 μmol g −1 h −1 under visible light, a remarkable 16‐fold increase compared to traditional BCN materials. The improvement is attributed to precise bandgap engineering; boron doping and nitrogen vacancies adjust the electronic structure, while the synergistic effects of Cu, P, and CNT enhance charge transfer dynamics. The ultrathin NiPc framework introduces atomically dispersed active sites, whereas a Z‐scheme‐driven charge separation mechanism facilitates efficient electron movement. This work, by integrating defect engineering, heterojunction design, and single‐atom catalysis, contributes to the advancement of photocatalytic nitrogen fixation, offering a scalable pathway for sustainable ammonia production. The results underscore the importance of multi‐component synergy in overcoming kinetic barriers, opening new avenues for energy‐efficient alternatives to conventional synthesis methods.

10.1016/j.ecmx.2026.102431.abstract: The potential of various metal oxides as redox carrier materials was investigated for on-demand hydrogen/ammonia production and solid-state storage through solar chemical-looping processes. Metal production involves solar-driven reduction assisted by various bio-sourced reductants, while nitride synthesis requires a similar reduction process supplemented by nitrogen incorporation. The reduced metals act as long-term solid storage media. Steam oxidation of metals (or nitrides) produces pure H 2 (or NH 3 ). A selection of oxide/metal and oxide/nitride pairs was carried out to identify the most promising systems. Suitable metals were screened according to multi-criteria: thermodynamic feasibility/conversion extents at equilibrium, cycle/process efficiencies, energy/exergy demands, specific storage density, and material availability/cost. Mo, W, and V offer high volumetric H 2 storage density despite low abundance and high cost. Al, Si, Mg, Fe, Mn, Cr, and Ti balance favorable storage performance with high availability and affordability, making them adapted for large-scale H 2 storage, while Zn, Sn, Ga, Ge, Ca, Sr, Ta, and Sc are less abundant or show moderate performance, suited mainly for niche uses. Regarding nitrides for NH 3 synthesis, AlN, TaN, ZrN, W 2 N, TiN, and Ge 3 N 4 formation from oxides with C/N 2 was thermodynamically feasible. Furthermore, energy and exergy analysis revealed that Fe(s), Mo(s), Sn(s), W(s) systems show maximum solar-to-fuel efficiencies (40–50% for C, 20–25% for CH 4 reductant), followed by Ga(g), Ge(s), Mn(g), V(g), Zn(g), Ta(s), and B(s). They also require the lowest exergy demand and inversion temperatures. In contrast, Al(g), Ca(g), Cr(g), Mg(g), Si(g), Sr(g), Ti(g), and Sc(s) show lower process efficiencies and higher exergy requirements due to higher temperatures and associated losses. The cycle temperatures could however be decreased in open reactor systems or by tuning the operating conditions to favor metals synthesis.

10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.131297.abstract: With cumulative spent lithium-ion battery (LIB) waste projected to exceed 11 million tonnes by 2030, rapid and low-carbon regeneration technologies are increasingly important for securing secondary resources. Joule heating provides heating and cooling rates of 103-105 K s-1 and millisecond-to-second thermal exposure, enabling impurity removal, lattice reconstruction and non-equilibrium defect regulation while limiting prolonged diffusion and side reactions. This review critically synthesizes Joule heating-enabled recycling, regeneration and upcycling of spent LIB anodes and cathodes, together with the underlying mechanisms, industrial barriers and environmental implications. Representative graphite-regeneration studies report >99% removal of Li and transition metal contaminants using only 0.1 M HCl, with regenerated or upcycled graphite delivering approximately 351-459 mAh·g-1. For cathodes, Joule heating direct regeneration restored spent LiCoO2 from 103.9 to 133 mAh·g-1 within 8 s. Quantitative TEA and LCA further indicate that representative graphite regeneration routes require approximately 1.05-15.38 MJ kg-1 and cost $1.48-5.79 kg-1, with greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions of up to 98% depending on the comparator and system boundary. Joule heating assisted cathode recycling has reported 72-82% lower GHG emissions than conventional benchmarks. However, most demonstrations remain at laboratory or gram scale. This review identifies spent graphite regeneration as the most immediately deployable field and cathode direct regeneration as a high-value but more feedstock-sensitive target, while emphasizing adaptive process control, transparent LCA/TEA boundaries and responsible scale-up as priorities for industrial translation.

10.1021/acsami.6c16760.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis while simultaneously addressing nitrate pollution in wastewater. However, the irreversible structural reconstruction commonly observed in catalysts during NO3RR obscures the true active sites and complicates mechanistic understanding. In this study, flower-like CuCo2S4 nanocrystals synthesized via a hot-injection method serve as a model ternary sulfide system to systematically probe reconstruction dynamics and identify active phases under operating conditions. Experimental characterizations reveal that CuCo2S4 gradually evolves into Cu-Co(OH)2/Co9S8 through electrochemical reconstruction. This reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent NO3RR performance, achieving an average Faradaic efficiency of 97.3%, an ammonia production rate of 363.1 μmol h–1 mg–1, and remarkable cycling stability. In situ FTIR spectra indicate that Cu incorporation promotes the conversion of *NO2 and accelerates subsequent hydrogenation steps. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that Cu doping facilitates *NH3 desorption and optimizes the balance between NO3– adsorption and *NH3 release. This work systematically deciphers the reconstruction pathway of sulfide catalysts during NO3RR, offering fundamental insights into electrocatalyst reconstruction mechanisms and providing a design strategy for high-performance ammonia-production electrocatalysts.

10.1021/acsanm.6c05096.abstract: Abstract Ammonia (NH3) is a representative reducing toxic gas whose rapid, low-concentration detection is important in constant-temperature, constant-humidity environments such as semiconductor cleanrooms, yet existing NH3 sensors often suffer from high operating temperatures or slow response/recovery kinetics. Fibrous phosphorus (FP), a layered allotrope of elemental phosphorus with a parallel tubular structure, is an appealing sensing candidate, but its efficient preparation and gas-sensing potential remain underexplored. Here, we report an iodine-assisted chemical vapor transport method that enables gram-scale synthesis of FP within 5 h with a yield exceeding 99%, without the need for precise temperature-gradient control. The key is the iodine-mediated cleavage of P4 cages and the directed assembly of active phosphorus fragments into tubular FP. Taking advantage of the weak interlayer van der Waals interactions, high-quality FP nanoribbons (FP-NRs) with an average width of ∼50 nm, an average length of ∼6 μm, and aspect ratios exceeding 150 for ∼60% of the ribbons are obtained by 60 min of ice-bath exfoliation. The FP-NRs sensor exhibits a high response of 826% toward 100 ppm NH3 at room temperature, with response/recovery times of 31/7 s under the 90% criterion, and remains responsive at 2 ppm NH3 (response 69.8%). When all tested gases are compared at the same concentration, the response to NH3 is significantly higher than that to the interfering gases. Combined DFT calculations and in situ FTIR/Raman measurements reveal that NH3 adsorption on FP is dominated by physical adsorption (adsorption energy −0.26 eV; Bader charge transfer ∼0.02 e), which accounts for the high sensitivity, selectivity, and fast recovery. This work provides a scalable route to FP nanoribbons and demonstrates their potential for practical room-temperature NH3 sensing.

10.1021/acscatal.6c07178.abstract: Abstract The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.

10.1021/acsestwater.6c01131.abstract: Abstract Predicting the ammonium nitrogen (NH4+-N) adsorption capacity of biochar is challenged by coupled, nonlinear interactions among operational variables, pyrolysis synthesis parameters, and intrinsic material properties. A unified data set comprising 425 literature-reported adsorption records from 18 studies was compiled, and preprocessing (KNN imputation and Z-score standardization) was fitted exclusively on the training subset to prevent data leakage. Among seven machine learning algorithms benchmarked with Bayesian optimization and 5-fold cross-validation, XGBoost achieved the highest test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.901 and root-mean-square error of 0.555 mg g–1. TreeSHAP analysis quantitatively decoupled three driver groups, adsorption operational parameters (53.3%), biochar physicochemical properties (38.2%), and pyrolysis synthesis parameters (8.5%), and identified initial concentration, biochar oxygen content, and adsorbent dosage as the dominant variables, with oxygen content exhibiting a unimodal relationship with adsorption capacity. Partial dependence plots were further utilized to reveal nonlinear response behaviors and determine data-coverage-validated optimal operation and design windows for key variables. A graphical user interface was developed to estimate equilibrium adsorption capacity, reducing reliance on extensive laboratory trials.

10.1021/jacs.6c14152.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic photocatalysis can enhance conventional chemical transformations, but macroscale kinetic metrics, such as overall reaction rates and apparent activation barriers, are insufficient to identify the specific elementary steps modulated by hot carriers, limiting precise control over catalytic reactivity and selectivity. Here, we apply a spectrokinetic strategy based on in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) to resolve elementary-step energetics in NH3 decomposition over CuRu alloy antenna–reactor catalysts. CuRu and Na-modified CuRu show different relative sensitivities to heating and illumination, providing a paired system for tracking how kinetic control is redistributed under thermal and plasmonic conditions. Temporal in situ DRIFTS and Arrhenius analysis identify site-dependent adsorbed N2 (*N2) intermediates and reveal a sequential migration–desorption pathway for *N2 removal. Thermal kinetic analysis shows that Na enhances thermocatalytic activity, despite strengthening *N2 binding and increasing the *N2 desorption barrier at terrace sites, while DFT calculations suggest that this enhancement is consistent with a reduced interfacial N–N coupling barrier. Under illumination, CuRu exhibits a nearly three-orders-of-magnitude light-specific rate enhancement, accompanied by decreases of 0.75 and 0.28 eV in the activation barriers for terrace *N2 desorption and interfacial *N2 migration, respectively, relative to dark thermal conditions. Comparing CuRu and CuRu–Na shows that illumination affects interfacial *N2 migration more selectively than terrace *N2 desorption, identifying interfacial *N2 removal as a site-sensitive step in plasmon-promoted active-site regeneration. These findings connect plasmonic excitation with site-dependent surface dynamics and elementary-step energetics, providing a framework for understanding how light redirects kinetic control in multistep catalysis.

10.1021/jacs.6c15718.abstract: Abstract Above 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, the hydrogen evolution reaction is thermodynamically suppressed, making this potential region attractive for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. However, in neutral and alkaline media typically used for the nitrate reduction reaction, protons for successive hydrogenation steps derive mainly from water dissociation, which becomes increasingly sluggish at more positive potentials. Proton availability thus governs the hydrogenation kinetics of nitrate and its intermediates. Using CuRu nanorods as a model catalyst, we resolve how the electrolyte and the catalyst jointly control the proton supply during NO3RR at positive potentials. Macroelectrode measurements reveal that the NO3– reduction kinetics depend on OH– concentration, and single-particle electrochemistry on a single CuRu nanorod, where ultrafast mass transport avoids local OH– accumulation, assigns this dependence to the bulk. Moreover, in situ scanning electrochemical microscopy shows that bulk OH– governs water dissociation kinetics; capacitance and potential-of-zero-charge measurements trace this to a strengthened, cation-enriched interfacial electric field, which accelerates water dissociation and sustains the proton supply at positive potentials. Building on the electrolyte-enhanced proton supply, Cu incorporation tunes the competitive adsorption between H2O-derived species and NO3– on the CuRu surface, thereby avoiding a proton oversupply that compromises the conversion kinetics. These results provide systematic insight into how bulk OH– concentration and catalyst composition cooperatively modulate proton supply, enhancing nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at HER-free potentials.

10.1021/photonsci.6c00065.abstract: Abstract This work presents the design, implementation, and validation of a custom-built in situ atomic layer deposition (ALD) reactor developed at the ALBA Synchrotron Light Source (Cerdanyola del Vallès, Spain), enabling direct integration with synchrotron X-ray beamlines. A modular configuration allows the ALD reactor to be deployed at two ALBA Synchrotron beamlines: NCD-SWEET beamline (BL11) for Grazing Incidence Small Angle X-ray Scattering (GISAXS) and NOTOS beamline (BL16) for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), requiring only minimal reconfiguration. The reactor performance was validated by in situ deposition of TiO2 thin films using titanium tetraisopropoxide (TTIP) and H2O as the precursor and co-reactant, respectively, with a growth per cycle (GPC) of 0.17 Å·cycle–1 at 150 °C. This system was chosen for its low growth rate, as a demanding test of detection sensitivity. In situ GISAXS revealed the continuous evolution of film morphology and near-surface electron density over 1000 ALD cycles, while in situ X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) quantitatively resolved three kinetically distinct growth regimes: prenucleation, nucleation development, and steady-state growth. The complementarity of the two techniques provides a comprehensive picture of ALD growth dynamics that neither technique could deliver independently, demonstrating the potential of the ALD system presented here for in situ multi-technique characterization of a broad range of ALD processes.

10.1149/1945-7111/aebcb9.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic reduction reaction of nitrate to ammonia (NO3RR) has emerged as a promising strategy that couples nitrate pollutant remediation with sustainable NH3 production. Practical nitrate-containing industrial wastewater usually presents a wide pH distribution range, which puts forward an urgent requirement for pH-adaptive NO₃RR catalysts with high ammonia selectivity. Conventional NO3RR catalysts fail to deliver high NH3 Faradaic efficiency under extreme acidic or alkaline conditions, mainly due to uncontrollable competitive adsorption of hydrogen intermediates on active sites. Herein, we report a ruthenium-decorated copper foam catalyst (RuCuF@PUS) fabricated via a facile two-step electrodeposition method, which achieves exceptional NO3RR performance across a wide pH window of 1-12. The interconnected porous framework enables efficient mass transfer, while the precisely designed dual active sites endow Cu with strong nitrate adsorption and activation capability, and Ru with accelerated sequential hydrogenation kinetics. In acidic condition, the catalyst achieves a remarkable ammonia yield rate of 457.56 µmol/h·cm2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE, with a peak Faradaic efficiency of 90.96%. Furthermore, a proof-of-concept alkaline-acidic hybrid Zn–NO3 battery assembled with the RuCuF@PUS cathode and real nitrate-containing wastewater as electrolyte achieves an open-circuit voltage of 1.29 V and a peak power density of 25.93 mW/cm2.

10.2118/235635-ms.abstract: Abstract Green ammonia projects face increasing challenges in progressing from conceptual development toward bankable execution, requiring coordinated development across technology, infrastructure, safety assurance, and commercial pathways. This paper presents the outcome of an ongoing front-end development program for a compact floating green ammonia FPSO-type facility. It discusses how mature technologies can be selected for floating applications, modularized, marinized, and integrated with safety-led design to support a scalable and bankable infrastructure model. The development incorporates contributions from the project developer, the design and fabrication contractor, and an independent classification and technical assurance partner. Market-driven design considerations include renewable power availability, geographical location, export route, and potential offtake markets. The technical scope includes approximately 500 MW renewable power intake, high-voltage distribution, hydrogen production, nitrogen generation, ammonia synthesis, refrigerated storage, utilities, marine systems, and offloading interfaces. Safety studies comprise HAZID, layout review, safety screening, and coarse quantitative risk assessment covering hydrogen and ammonia major accident hazards, including hydrogen accumulation and explosion risk, ammonia toxic dispersion, compact layout constraints, marine offloading interfaces, and nearshore risk exposure. The paper demonstrates how technical readiness, commercial readiness, and safety and regulatory readiness can be matured together to progress the concept beyond Approval in Principle toward an execution-ready project definition.

10.2118/235870-ms.abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are flammable and some of them are hazardous to human health. Apart from its toxic nature, VOCs can also take part into photochemical reactions and contribute to formation of ozone and fine particles, causing detrimental influences on atmospheric quality. Increase in VOCs emission from human activity has been recognized as primary causes of urban air pollution in China, and targeted control and constant removal of VOCs was proposed as key measures to mitigate atmosphere problems. Petrochemical facility was significant emission sources for VOCs and NOx and represents an possibility of co-treatment of these two pollutants. In this work, treatment of petrochemical VOCs by directing VOCs stream into facility heater or process furnace was proposed and confirmed. The oxidation of VOCs and its influence on NOx conversion was probed within an experimental setup, simulating the co-conversion process of petrochemical VOCs and NOx. The propane and propylene were selected as representatives of petrochemical VOCs and used as reactant with a feed ratio of 2% and 0.5% (V/V %). NO was chosen to act as NOx at feeding concentration of 200 and 800 mg/m3. Air stream was also feed to simulate oxidative condition within the process furnace or incinerator. Influences of VOCs species, temperature and concentration on NOx conversion were confirmed. The results suggest that reduction of NO takes place in the presence of VOCs at temperature higher than 300°C regardless of NO concentration. The VOCs species selectively reduce NO below 500°C while it was gradually oxidized by oxygen as temperature further increases and was completely consumed above 700°C. Lower temperature favors NO reduction by VOCs compared with high temperature (above 600°C). An optimum temperature window (400~600°C) was obtained for NO conversion by VOCs and more than 30% NO can be reduced by VOCs. Concentration of VOCs also play an important role in NO reduction. Increase in ratio of VOCs facilitate NO reduction. Alkane seems to be more reactive in NO reduction than alkene. According to finding in this work, it was advised that the alkane VOCs stream was routed into latter stage of process furnace with temperature lower than 700°C where NOx has been formed. In case of alkene and aromatic VOCs stream, a higher temperature was needed and the former furnace stage was more preferred. In the first time, co-treatment of VOCs and NOx in petrochemical facility was proposed. The feasibility and performance were subsequently confirmed in lab scale setup. The information obtained in this study improves our understanding on VOCs conversion in process furnace and its influence on in-site NOx reduction. Targeted suggestion was formulated which can promote the progresses in VOCs abatement in China.

10.26434/chemrxiv-2024-p1txk/v2.abstract: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size. In pure γ-alumina, this early saturation, together with retention of the ordered mesostructure, is consistent with geometrically constrained crystallite growth. Magnesium incorporation enables further crystallite enlargement before saturation, yielding larger defect-spinel-related domains while retaining long-range mesoscopic order. We further demonstrate the incorporation of in situ crystallized platinum nanoparticles within the ordered magnesium-aluminum oxide framework and their activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation at 350 °C. These results demonstrate that ultrafast Joule heating can access distinct crystallization trajectories in compositionally modified mesoporous oxides that are precluded by mesostructural collapse during conventional furnace heating.

10.26434/chemrxiv.15011542/v1.abstract: This study compares the alternating-magnetic-field (AMF) heating of Fe3O4-, MnFe2O4-, MgFe2O4-, and SrFe12O19-targeted nanoparticle preparations and of their sequentially silica-modified, aminated, Aufunctionalized, and PEG-treated forms. The compositions are identified by their nominal synthesis precursors. Temperature–time curves and the times required to reach 42 °C were measured in water and in nominally 1% agar phantoms under identical induction-generator settings (132 kHz; 5 kW rated output). Among the untreated preparations, the Mg-labeled series reached 42 °C fastest (145 s in water and 187 s in agar), whereas the Srlabeled series was the slowest (222 and 293 s, respectively). For the Mg-labeled particles, increasing the concentration from 2.5 to 10 mg mL 1 shortened the time to 42 °C from 394 to 77 s in water and from 381 to 112 - s in agar. In water, the aminated Mn-, Mg-, and Sr-labeled samples heated fastest within their respective surfacetreatment series (139, 124, and 209 s), whereas the unmodified Fe-labeled core was fastest within the Fe series (171 s). The PEG-treated specimens exhibited the longest times in all four water-based series. FTIR, SEM, and EDX analyses characterized the successive surface-treatment stages, including the detection of Au after functionalization. Together, these findings clarify how precursor-defined ferrite composition, concentration, surface treatment, and surrounding medium influence magnetic heating under matched apparatus conditions.

10.3389/fceng.2026.1966277.abstract: The high temperature water-gas shift (HT-WGS) reaction is a central conversion step in ammonia production since it boosts the hydrogen yield and reduces the carbon monoxide content in the synthesis gas mixture before subsequent purification and ammonia synthesis. The industrial reactor was analyzed numerically with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. A three-dimensional model was created by combining momentum transport, heat transfer, multicomponent species transport, heterogeneous reaction kinetics, and intraparticle diffusion in porous Fe-Cr catalyst pellets under realistic adiabatic plant operating conditions. The novelty of the approach lies in combining industrial plant validation with simultaneous representation of reactor scale transport and pellet -scale diffusion-reaction processes. The model predictions were compared with the measured axial temperature profile and outlet gas composition obtained from the industrial plant. The model accurately predicted plant data with MAE = 3.50 K, R 2 = 0.950 (temperatures), and MAPE = 5.30% (outlet content). The validated model was used to examine velocity, temperature, pressure, gas-composition, gas–pellet concentration, and intraparticle concentration profiles. A parametric analysis was performed to evaluate the effects of inlet temperature and steam-to-CO ratio on CO conversion. The pressure profile demonstrated an approximately linear decrease across the catalyst bed, dropping from 30 to 28.35 bar. The mole fractions of CO and H 2 O dropped along the reactive bed, while CO 2 and H 2 rose. Increasing the inlet temperature enhanced CO conversion from about 38.5% at 618 K to around 71% at 653–658 K, while increasing the steam-to-CO ratio from 4.0 to 6.0 improved anticipated conversion from approximately 50%–70%. The validated model is a valuable tool for assessing the operation of industrial HT-WGS reactors in ammonia producing facilities.

10.3390/molecules31213938.abstract: The development of sustainable fuels and hydrogen carriers is essential for a carbon-neutral energy future. Ammonia (NH3) is a promising energy vector, yet its synthesis remains dependent on the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, while nitrogen oxides (NOx) persist as major atmospheric pollutants. In this work, spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the MPWB1K/def2SVP level are used to investigate the capture and reduction of NO and NO2 within a rigid covalent organic framework (M1). Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shift (NICS) analysis reveals a strongly aromatic shielding character (NICS = −10.8) that provides a unique electronic environment, while electrostatic potential (ESP) mapping illustrates local electron density. Confinement within the framework suppresses competing pathways that preferentially favor the pathway toward NH3 and H2O. Activation barriers are significantly reduced, driven by charge transfer that weakens N–O bonds. The rigid covalent organic framework remains structurally stable throughout the process. These findings demonstrate a viable strategy for converting atmospheric pollutants into valuable energy carriers under moderate thermal activation.

10.3390/pr14213539.abstract: Joule heating coupled with porous media offers rapid in situ heat generation and a more uniform temperature distribution for DRM reactions, whereas the strong coupling of structural and operating parameters renders conventional trial-and-error optimization inefficient and costly. To tackle this challenge, a multi-physics numerical model for a centrally resistively heated DRM reactor is constructed by coupling Joule heating, flow and heat transfer, multicomponent species transport, and apparent reaction kinetics. A fully connected feedforward neural network (FC-FNN) surrogate model is further established to enable rapid prediction of reactor performance. Seven critical input variables are selected, including reaction temperature, gas hourly space velocity (GHSV), etc., and 9216 simulation samples are generated via numerical simulations for surrogate model training and parametric analysis. The results demonstrate that the Bayesian-optimized FC-FNN model exhibits high predictive accuracy for the core reactor performance metrics, achieving coefficients of determination (R2) above 0.960 for CH4 conversion, CO2 conversion, energy efficiency, and the H2/CO molar ratio. Subsequently, an unknown-constrained alternating Bayesian optimization (UCA-BO) algorithm is adopted to maximize the average reactant conversion under the constraints of H2/CO molar ratio ≥ 0.9 and bed-temperature non-uniformity ≤ 5%. Under the optimized operating conditions, the average reactant conversion reaches 94.12%, accompanied by a H2/CO molar ratio of 0.98, a bed-temperature non-uniformity of 4.53%, and a system energy efficiency of 74.83%. Posterior verification with the trained surrogate model gives slightly lower values (91.28%, 0.91, 4.86%, and 72.36%), all of which remain within the imposed constraints, confirming feasibility. Overall, the proposed integrated framework of numerical simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization enables efficient parameter screening and comprehensive performance optimization of resistively heated porous-media DRM systems, providing a methodological basis for the structural design and operating-parameter optimization of related reactor systems.

10.3390/systems14111407.abstract: Renewable power fluctuations and uncertain ammonia synthesis performance complicate operational coordination in green hydrogen–ammonia systems. This study develops a closed-loop prediction–scheduling framework using dual Gaussian processes to characterize renewable power and process performance. Calibrated lower and upper bounds enter material and energy constraints, while multi-objective particle swarm optimization balances operating cost and schedule variation. A joint-risk index selects plan retention, local repair, or global re-optimization, combined with plan refresh and conditional Pareto reuse in rolling horizon scheduling. The framework is evaluated with 24 h aggregated simulations using public meteorological data and published experimental data. Paired comparisons across seven fixed scenarios show that event-triggered and periodic scheduling both completed all 20 runs per scenario while satisfying all hard constraints. Under the reported serial timing protocol, event triggering reduced total controller runtime by 15.30–34.73%. Of 234 supplementary stress-test requests, 177 completed the day, including 176 that satisfied all hard constraints and one with a terminal audit failure; 57 stopped during the search. These results show that the framework coordinates probabilistic prediction, physical constraints, and scheduling responses under the specified simulation conditions, providing a reproducible approach to operational optimization of green hydrogen–ammonia systems.
